### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **83** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4df174bcc48d694e654f90105ebd9e68d3545136`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **156** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4df174bcc48d694e654f90105ebd9e68d3545136` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `16cf9bd1f14b8d30d5fb3516f1692be47d454130` — the merge of head `225d5bc02c4dcb441fd812288de8209d98192a48` into base `4df174bcc48d694e654f90105ebd9e68d3545136`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 16cf9bd1f14b8d30d5fb3516f1692be47d454130 && git checkout 16cf9bd1f14b8d30d5fb3516f1692be47d454130
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4df174bcc48d694e654f90105ebd9e68d3545136 225d5bc02c4dcb441fd812288de8209d98192a48 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4df174bcc48d694e654f90105ebd9e68d3545136 && git merge --no-ff 225d5bc02c4dcb441fd812288de8209d98192a48

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4df174bcc48d694e654f90105ebd9e68d3545136
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4df174bcc48d694e654f90105ebd9e68d3545136` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The rest of the diff (the regenerated reference mdx under content/docs/references, the remaining unit tests, the resolver and assembly test cells) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

Stage 2 of ruling B. Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged against the ruling's channel list (shares incl. share links, sharing rules, position and permission-set grants with their RLS evaluated; never the internal OWD baseline, the `everyone` default sets or the member directory) and the scope note's three items.

1. **Spec prose (the hits) — right.** `ExecutionContextSchema.audience`'s docblock and `AuthzPostureSchema`'s `.describe` move from "explicitly shared rows only" to the ruled channel list, the owner_only floor and the BU-tree exclusion. The enums are unchanged; no key added or removed; the `.describe` change re-renders in the generated reference pages, which are regenerated in the diff (Build Docs and Spec property liveness green). The prose states exactly what the code below does.

2. **Audience and posture (`resolve-authz-context.ts`, `posture-ladder.ts`, `assemble-execution-context.ts`) — right.** `holdsExternalIdentity(grants.positions)` (stage 1's projection of `sys_member.role = external` to `org_external`, per organization, fail-closed with no active organization) is the one input: it sets `grants.audience = 'external'` and `isExternal` into `derivePosture`, which returns `EXTERNAL` after `PLATFORM_ADMIN` and before `TENANT_ADMIN`. Precedence judged right: E5 refuses `external` beside `owner`/`admin`, so an org-admin grant can reach an external only as an explicit grant, and the ruling keeps "EXTERNAL is not a restricted MEMBER"; the unscoped platform grant stays deployment standing. Every holder therefore gets both stamps, through the one resolver every transport uses; `ENTRY_EXECUTION_CONTEXT_FIELDS` already carried `audience` (it was the `undefined` placeholder), so the assembled context now carries `authz.audience` on the human face and on the agent envelope (the human's population, intersected by plugin-sharing's delegator leg); a guest never carries it. No pre-existing `'EXTERNAL'` reader in non-test source outside core wakes up (grep: `external-owd-floor.ts`, the ladder constant, `derivePosture`, and the reference model's `case 'EXTERNAL'` are the only ones), so making the rung live activates no dormant deny branch elsewhere.

3. **The OWD seam (`external-owd-floor.ts`, `sharing-service.ts`, `external-owd-grant-stamp.ts`, step 2.6, `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts`) — right.** `owdForAudience` returns `'private'` for an external on every non-private effective model (`read`, `public`, and the model-less system default) unless the operation context carries a stamp naming THIS object for THIS class; it is applied in `buildReadFilter`, `buildWriteFilter`, `checkEdit` and `checkDelete`, after the guest deny-all. The stamp is produced where the grants resolve: step 2.6 of the CRUD middleware on the live `opCtx.context` (only when `isExternalAudienceContext`, so an internal principal is byte-unchanged), and as a patch on every rebuilt context handed to a sharing gate (read filter, canEdit, write verdict, explain). The predicate counts only a `using` clause on a held set's policy, excluding the object's `defaultRowScope` (`isObjectDefaultRowScopePolicy`) and the ownership floor (`isPlatformOwnershipFloorPolicy`, keyed on object+name+using so the new `external_default` copies are excluded too); the write class borrows from `select` as Layer 1 does, the read class never borrows. A stamp is object-named, class-separated, and `stampExternalGrant` deletes a stale one. I read `external_default`'s full policy list at the head: every `using` policy is object-specific (`auditLedgerRowScope` is `sys_audit_log` only); the only `object: '*'` policies are the two floor copies, which the provenance key excludes. So the floor lifts only where a grant's RLS genuinely speaks, which is the ruling's "with their RLS evaluated" sentence made mechanical (#25234's dependency).
   **"Exactly its explicit grants, nothing by default", enumerated:** no grant → `external_default` alone → own identity rows (own `sys_user`/`sys_member`; `sys_team_member`, `sys_account`, the two OAuth token tables fall to their objects' own `_self` `defaultRowScope`, read at the head), and the CRUD gate refuses every other object (matrix: `private_obj`, `platform_global` denied). A grant with no RLS on a public object → the object opens, rows are own + shared (dogfood supplierA: 2 of 4). A grant with RLS → the object's model stands, the RLS bounds the rows (dogfood supplierC: exactly 1; matrix stamp cells on the real middleware). The posture-ladder reference model is rewritten to the same three sources (own, shared, grant-visible, in-org only) and EXTERNAL ⊆ MEMBER still holds by construction.

4. **Write floor on `external_default` (`default-permission-sets.ts`) — right, and owed although the order did not name it.** Without `owner_only_writes`/`owner_only_deletes` bound to `org_external`, an external's by-id write on an object its grant opened reached every row while a member's stopped at its own (the dev's I2): the EXTERNAL ⊆ MEMBER nesting broken on writes. Same name/object/using as the member floor, so provenance and every relief apply identically; the floor is position-bound, so no member resolves it. `platform-ownership-policies.test.ts` now dedupes by identity key and pins the two carriers.

5. **Explain and describe (`external-baseline.ts`, `explain-engine.ts`, `security-plugin-explain-access.ts`, `resolveFallbackPermissionSets`) — right.** One helper (`humanBaselineFor`) names the baseline for the three readers that must agree (data plane, explainer attribution, describe fallback), so an external's baseline is `external_default`, attributed "external baseline (org_external)", and the member path is `[...configured]` (a copy; nothing compares by reference). Explain's OWD layer reports "owner_only for an external principal" through the SAME `grantRowPolicySpeaks` over the SAME `collectRLSPolicies`, so the report cannot disagree with the query. Explain's context from `buildContextForUser` now carries `audience`.

6. **Directory doors (`external-directory-door.ts`, `auth-manager.ts`) — right, scope-note items 1–3 closed.** `list-teams` and `get-full-organization.teams` answer an external only the teams it sits on (`sys_team_member`, read under system context); `list-invitations` only its own email, case-insensitive; a failed role read withholds everything (`withholdAll`, members/total/invitations/teams or the bare array), a failed team read keeps no team, a missing email keeps no invitation; the organization judged is the one the rows name, then the query, then the active org, so a member elsewhere is unchanged there. The docblock line on `includes('external')` vs exactly `'external'` is present and states E5 as the reason they agree. `ExternalDirectoryDoorDeps` gains a required `readUserTeamIds`; the module is not re-exported from plugin-auth's index, so this is not a published surface.

7. **The access matrix (`authz-matrix-gate.test.ts`) — right.** The EXTERNAL column at Layers 0 and 1: `task` read walled to the org and write `AND created_by = me` (the floor, now from `external_default`), `private_obj` and `platform_global` CRUD-denied, `better_auth` own row only; the ladder-order check adds `external` at the foot; the stamp is measured end to end on the real middleware (no-RLS grant → not stamped; RLS grant → stamped read and derived write; stale stamp cleared; member never stamped).

8. **An ordinary member is byte-for-byte unchanged — right.** `owdForAudience` returns the model untouched for a non-external context; step 2.6 stamps only inside `isExternalAudienceContext`; the door's `NARROWED_PATHS` branch returns before any mutation for a non-external caller; `derivePosture` with `isExternal` absent is the old function; `audience` stays `undefined` for a member exactly as before; `humanBaselineFor` returns the configured list for every non-external human. CONTROL cells are pinned in every new test file and in the dogfood boot (member reads all four rows, both teams, both invitations, the whole directory).

9. **Residual paths to the member directory or team names, enumerated:** (a) `sys_user`/`sys_member` at the data door — own row (stage 1, unchanged); (b) `sys_team` — not granted by `external_default`; (c) `sys_team_member` — the object's own `_self` default scope, own rows; (d) the four better-auth doors — narrowed; (e) `list-team-members` — not narrowed, see ③; (f) an administrator binding `member_default`/`viewer_readonly` or a `sys_team` grant to an external — an explicit grant, which the ruling admits. No unintended path found.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/25233-external-posture-owd-floor.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` — exactly the five published packages with source changes (qa/dogfood is private; docs are not a package). It carries both declaration lines. `Check Changeset` green.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — judged right. Published additions: core exports `EXTERNAL_READ_GRANT_KEY`, `EXTERNAL_WRITE_GRANT_KEY`, `isExternalAudienceContext`, `externalGrantSpeaks`, `owdForAudience`; optional `PostureEvidence.isExternal`, optional `ResolvedAuthzContext.audience` / `UserAuthzGrants.audience`, optional `ExplainEngineDeps.externalGrantSpeaks`. Narrowings (the OWD floor, the write floor, the doors) reach only holders of the `external` role; stage 1's `.changeset/25233-external-org-role.md` is still pending on `origin/main` (read in the tree), so no release has shipped a holder to narrow. Two edges judged and accepted: (i) `POSTURE_INJECTION_RULE.EXTERNAL`'s string value changes — documentary prose on an exported constant, within `minor`; (ii) a hand-built context carrying `audience: 'external'` is now floored where before nothing read the key — that is the key's documented meaning becoming enforced (the design round measured zero consumers), not a contract break. `Metadata-protocol: semantic` — right: nothing an author writes is added or refused; `sharingModel` on an object and `rowLevelSecurity.using` on a set gain a meaning for external holders. The level follows the kind: `minor` on every moved package.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (PR body and report 6375701518), each answered:

- **Open question — "access matrix": the authz-matrix-gate EXTERNAL column, or the ADR-0090 D6 explain matrix?** Judged: **the authz-matrix-gate column; the dev's reading is right and no follow-up is owed.** The maintainer's 「25233 选择 B」 adopts option B as the dev's report states it, whose words are "the OWD seam and matrix cells" — "cells" is this repo's word for the `authz-matrix-gate` snapshot (`posture-ladder.ts`: "the real behavior guard is the `authz-matrix-gate` unit snapshot + the dogfood conformance matrix"; the gate's own retired D3 comment spoke of "EXTERNAL × layer … cells"). The ruling's restatement lists "the EXTERNAL column of the access matrix **and the explainers**" as two things, so the matrix is not the explain surface. ADR-0090 D6's `AccessMatrix` is `@objectstack/lint`'s metadata-only permissionSet × object snapshot, and D11 says audience is a property of the principal, never of the object; D11's "external-audience column" sentence rode `externalSharingModel`, retired in spec 18 and marked superseded by the 2026-10-14 note. With no per-object external metadata left, a metadata-only snapshot has nothing to put in such a column. The Tier H docs PR amending D11 should retire that sentence explicitly.

- **Out of scope 1 — a share on a public object is refused as inert, closing an external's share channel there.** Judged: **a follow-up with its own card, needing a ruling; not a stage-2 defect.** Read at the head: `inertGrantReason` refuses when `effectiveSharingModel` is `'public'` (that is `public_read_write`, `controlled_by_parent`, and a model-less `sys_*` object) or there is no `owner_id`; it does NOT refuse `public_read` (`'read'`), so the dev's note overstates the closed set and the dogfood's direct insert on a `public_read` object was not forced by this gate. On the closed set, the gate's premise ("a share row on it would never be consulted", decided caller-free by design, #8207 / ADR-0111 D7) is now false for one population: this PR's floor DOES consult share rows for an external on those objects (pinned in `external-owd-floor.test.ts`, share `s1` on the `public_read_write` `board`). Existing rows are honoured; minting new ones is refused for every recipient, and since `assertNotInertGrant` runs for system callers too, sharing-rule materialisation on those objects is refused as well. So two of the ruling's three channels cannot be provisioned on `public_read_write` / `controlled_by_parent` / model-less system objects; the grant-RLS channel (hotsrm's shape) and shares on `private` / `public_read` objects work, and the direction is fail-closed. Making an object-level inertness verdict audience-aware reverses a recorded decision, so it takes a ruling. Until it lands, `sharing-rules.mdx`'s "a manual share or a sharing rule" bullet overstates the external's reach on those objects by one clause; the follow-up card should carry that doc line.

- **Out of scope 2 — `list-team-members` stays membership-only.** Judged: **measure first; a `domain:services` follow-up (triage 6345105238's directory-doors card), not stage-2 blocking.** The two seat statements contradict each other: the stage-1 review (6371057486) read the door as requiring the caller on the team; the stage-2 report reads it as membership-only. better-auth's dist is not present in this container either, so I could not settle it. If membership-only, the exposure is teamMember rows (userId, teamId) of a team whose id the external already knows — ids only, since `sys_user` is own-row and `list-members` is narrowed, and team ids are no longer enumerable (`list-teams` narrowed, `sys_team` not granted). Neither E2 nor the scope note names this door. If better-auth already requires team membership, there is nothing to do.

- **`list-invitations` — measured, and with what result?** Yes. The dev measured `crud-invites.mjs` `listInvitations` in better-auth 1.7.12 as `findMemberByOrgId` only (membership-only) and narrowed it. Not re-readable here, but the fact is pinned on a real boot by the dogfood CONTROL: a plain `member` is answered both fixture invitations (`invitations.length >= 2`), which only a membership-only door does, and the external is answered its own only, another external `[]`. The dogfood project includes `test/**/*.test.ts`, and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on this head, so CI measured it.

- **Write floor outside the order; `platform-ownership-policies.ts` docblock and `sharing-rules.mdx` outside the file list:** accepted (① item 4; the docblock and the doc state what the code does).
- **Pins moved (floor dedupe by identity key; posture-ladder dataset gains `r6`; matrix ladder order):** each read; each is the derived consequence of ① items 3, 4 and 7.
- **An edge the PR pins but the ruling's sentence does not literally cover:** an object with no `owner_id` in its fields and a public effective model is "not under OWD" for every principal, so an external holding an RLS-less grant on it reads every row (`external-owd-floor.test.ts`, the `ownerless` case). In practice `applySystemFields` injects `owner_id` into registered business objects and every system object `external_default` names is own-row-scoped by its own `defaultRowScope`, so the case needs an administrator's explicit grant on an author-declared ownerless object. Accepted as the stated limit; the Tier H ADR text should name it (or the follow-up may deny-all externals there absent a speaking grant).
- **Explain's guest → EXTERNAL debugger mapping** now shares the rung's name with a live population; harmless (the guest deny-all precedes every sharing gate), noted for the ADR text.
- `#25234` PR ② serial constraint: whichever lands second merges main — accepted as declared.
